name: Sacituzumab govitecan
drug_class: Anti-TROP2 antibody–drug conjugate (topoisomerase I inhibitor payload)
route_note: IV infusion on days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycles

discovery.note: Humanised anti-TROP2 antibody hRS7 linked by a hydrolysable CL2A linker to SN-38, the active metabolite of irinotecan.

tagline: First TROP2-directed ADC, approved for metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
summary: Sacituzumab govitecan is an antibody–drug conjugate that targets TROP2, a surface glycoprotein found on many epithelial cancers, and delivers SN-38. It is approved for metastatic triple-negative and HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer after prior therapy.
mechanism: The antibody binds TROP2 (TACSTD2), and the conjugate releases SN-38 both after internalisation and in the tumour microenvironment through hydrolysis of the linker.
SN-38 inhibits topoisomerase I, causing DNA strand breaks and cell death. Its membrane permeability allows a bystander effect on neighbouring tumour cells. The drug-to-antibody ratio is about 7.6.
uses: Unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after two or more prior therapies
HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer after endocrine therapy and chemotherapy

history.title: Accelerated approval
history.detail: FDA grants accelerated approval in April for metastatic TNBC.

history.title: Gilead acquisition
history.detail: Gilead acquires Immunomedics for about $21 billion.

history.title: ASCENT and full approval
history.detail: ASCENT shows a survival benefit over chemotherapy; FDA converts to regular approval and the EU approves Trodelvy.

history.title: Urothelial cancer
history.detail: Accelerated approval for metastatic urothelial carcinoma, later withdrawn in 2024 after the confirmatory trial failed.

history.title: HR-positive breast cancer
history.detail: Approved for HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer after TROPiCS-02.

pk.metabolism: SN-38 glucuronidated by UGT1A1 to SN-38G

safety.boxed_warning: Severe or life-threatening neutropenia and severe diarrhoea.

facts: People homozygous for UGT1A1*28 have higher risk of neutropenia because they glucuronidate SN-38 more slowly.
TROP2 is expressed on most triple-negative breast cancers, so testing for the target is not required.
